The communication problem
The audience needs to understand source, ingredient, taste, serving and practical use before 
paying a premium. High production quality should support a clear explanation and a useful 
response when the customer asks a question.
The brief identifies low confidence in supplements and a higher-price objection. A polished film can 
suggest care, but it cannot establish ingredient quality on its own. Make the explanation and the 
evidence path easy to find. A source question requires the applicable product document. A taste 
question needs a practical demonstration or an accurate account of what the customer can 
expect. A price question needs a clear account of the product, quantity and role. The April 2024 
protein study provides relevant category context after its publication, but it is not a product-
specific test of TruNativ. Keep that distinction in any research or founder explanation.
The programme answers source, ingredient, taste, serving and price questions through 
explanations the customer can check. Premium images support care while founder answers, 
customer experience and useful comments carry accountability.

Edit, motion and short rules
Conversation assembly
Mark story boundaries and repeated setup. Keep interruptions that carry meaning. Remove dead space 
after evaluating both speakers. Avoid a reaction from another moment when it changes the implied 
response. Before inserts, review the dialogue-only assembly for continuity.
Camera-switching proposal
Use a single when one host holds the account. Move to the two-shot when overlap, interruption or a 
shared reaction carries the exchange. Retain a source-continuous reaction when it changes the 
meaning. Record the camera-switch exceptions in the edit notes with source timecode.
Motion proposal and timing test
Proposed test at 30 fps: 6–10 frames for entrance, at least 2 seconds of legible hold for a short label, 
and 6–8 frames for exit. Final timings depend on shot frame rate, speech and copy length. Keep the text 
stable during the hold. Review at full frame and portrait scale. These numbers are proposed test values.
Portrait edit and captions
Check the two-shot before selecting a crop. Use a split layout only when both simultaneous reactions 
matter. Avoid covering mouths or programme references. Run a manual spelling pass for names, comics 
and sponsors. Export a clean portrait master, a captioned master and a sidecar caption file.
Source cue record
Every cue records episode ID, source media ID, real start/end timecode, spoken trigger, graphic copy, 
asset source, rights status and review decision. Leave timecodes open until the editor has the actual 
media. A published episode description supplies topics and metadata, not a dialogue transcript or a cut 
order.

Naming and recognition

The shopper first needs to recognise the range and then choose the relevant product. The word

name while its descriptor and green colour establish the source difference. Test recognition at shelf

Lettering construction

Script and scene order
Sweets
Interior home. A close view establishes the sweet and the husband’s attention. He asks through 
expression and a small persuasive gesture. The wife gives a matter-of-fact response. Keep a clear 
eyeline from the food to the partner. The husband’s disappointment follows the response, with a 
hold that allows the audience to register the exchange.
Birthday
Interior celebration. Establish a cake large enough to support the husband’s expectation. He 
anticipates a generous treat while the family celebration continues around him. A covered serving 
tray arrives. The lid lifts to reveal a tiny portion. Show the scale contrast before cutting to his face. 
His response turns the occasion into the next small disappointment.
Tea
Interior home. The husband lifts the cup and takes the first sip. Let the taste action complete. His 
expression changes into disappointment. Keep the partner or service reaction brief and preserve 
the main eyeline. The cup provides a new familiar situation while carrying the same recurring 
frustration.
Newspaper and preparation
Interior home and kitchen. The husband settles behind the newspaper. In the kitchen, the wife 
prepares kheer. Put Everyday Sweet into the practical preparation, with a readable carton insert and 
the applicable quantity from the approved serving copy. Return to the waiting husband as the bowl 
enters the scene. The newspaper lowers or lifts enough to reveal the food and motivate his next 
look.
Taste and close
The husband hesitates, then tries a spoonful. Give the first taste time to register before the change 
into enjoyment. The wife’s small reassurance completes the exchange. Extend the proposition 
through selected familiar use actions. Close on the red carton and approved product information, 
then retain the couple’s warmth in the final composition. Music and practical sound carry the tone. 
No spoken dialogue is required.

SW02  |  Everyday Sweet
SW02  /  7
Sweets and birthday direction
The sweet request
The opening should establish a familiar object quickly. Food styling needs an inviting surface and a 
consistent spoon or serving position. The husband’s request should feel like a small negotiation. Ask 
him to direct the intention towards his partner, then protect the look back towards the sweet. The 
wife responds economically. Avoid simultaneous large reactions, which would make it harder to 
know whose action changes the scene.
Shoot a shared view that establishes the relationship, a clean food insert and each actor’s reaction. 
Hold the spoon or bowl position after the selected action so the insert can match the wider take. 
Record the reaction with a little space before and after it. The editor should be able to extend the 
disappointment without repeating a gesture. The opening must remain intelligible before music or 
graphics are added.
The birthday portion joke
The cake and the tray provide the information. Begin with a readable birthday setting and a cake 
that supports the expectation. The family background supplies the occasion, while the husband 
remains the main point of attention. Direct the supporting cast to continue a restrained celebration 
around the central action. Their gestures should not hide the tray or draw the eye away when the lid 
moves.
Prepare a large covered tray with the tiny cake portion in a repeatable position. Test the insert on 
the intended screen so the portion size is immediately apparent. The camera needs to see the lid 
clear the food. Hold on the revealed tray before cutting to the husband’s reaction. Capture a 
slightly longer and a shorter reaction take. Maintain the same crumbs, portion orientation, candle 
state and tray position when returning to the wider view. The humour should come from the 
expectation and visible difference, with sound supplying a small accent.

SW02  |  Everyday Sweet
SW02  /  8
Tea and newspaper direction
The first sip
The tea scene continues the frustration through a new action. Establish the cup and the husband’s 
ordinary expectation. Ask the actor to complete the sip before showing disappointment. The 
change should be readable in the face without an additional explanatory gesture. Keep the cup, 
hand and partner eyelines consistent across the shared view, insert and reaction. The supporting 
response is a short beat that confirms the situation and returns attention to the husband.
The prop team should maintain drink level and a practical temperature between takes. Use matched 
cups where duplicates are needed. Record a clean lift, first sip, cup return and an uninterrupted 
performance take. The editor can then decide whether the action plays best in one shot or through 
an insert and reaction. Cup and saucer sound should remain restrained. It should help the practical 
action register without turning every movement into a gag.
The newspaper pause
The newspaper provides a quiet visual reset after the repeated disappointments. It gives the 
husband a simple activity and a surface that can hide the incoming bowl for the reveal. Work 
through the paper action in rehearsal. The actor needs to know where the bowl will arrive and how 
much of the face should be visible before the next look. Keep the paper’s folded state consistent in 
the selected sequence.
Record the bowl arriving as part of the wider action and as a clean insert. Test a table-height angle 
against a view that shows the newspaper moving out of the way. The preferred route should let the 
audience understand what has changed before the husband reacts. Protect a clean background 
and a complete reveal action. The quietness of this setup gives the kheer taste room to feel 
different from the earlier interruptions. Use the pause to establish anticipation, then move into the 
first spoonful.
